# Copilot instructions for this repository

## What this is

An [SWC](https://swc.rs) plugin (compiled to WebAssembly) that de-indents
template literals at compile time. Given a template literal preceded by a
`/** #__DE-INDENT__ */` (configurable) block comment, it removes the common
leading indentation from every line, so multi-line strings can be written
indented in source but rendered flush-left at runtime. This is the actual
Rust crate; it is distributed to consumers only as a compiled `.wasm` binary
via npm (see Publishing below), never as a published Rust crate.

## Build, test, lint

This is a Rust/npm project. The Rust fixture suite checks the native transform;
the Wasm suite checks the compiled artifact through the SWC host:

- `cargo build --locked` -- native dev build (for iterating on the algorithm/tests).
- `npm run test:rust` (= `cargo test --locked`) -- runs unit tests and the Rust
  raw/TS fixture suites.
- `npm run test:swc` -- builds the Wasm artifact and runs every TS fixture
  through `@swc/core`, with a hard per-fixture subprocess timeout.
- `npm test` -- runs both the Rust and Wasm suites.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` -- must be clean; CI enforces this.
- Rust 1.98.1 is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and used in the devcontainer,
  CI, and publishing workflow. Keep those toolchains aligned; the floating
  nightly used for 1.5.1 produced a Wasm artifact that hangs in SWC.
- `cargo build-wasi --locked --release` (= `npm run build`) -- builds the actual
  publishable plugin artifact for `wasm32-wasip1`. This alias is defined in
  `.cargo/config.toml`; there's also a `build-wasm32` alias for
  `wasm32-unknown-unknown` if needed. The pinned toolchain includes the
  `wasm32-wasip1` target.
- `npm run prepack` runs the Wasm suite before npm packages the artifact.

### Running a single test

Unit tests in `src/utils.rs` are normal `#[test]` fns, runnable the usual way,
e.g. `cargo test test_get_indentation_only_indentation`.

Fixture tests (see Testing below) are generated by the `#[testing::fixture(...)]`
macro from file paths, producing names like
`fixture_space_tests__fixture__raw__space__clamp__input_txt`. You don't need
the full name -- `cargo test` filters by substring, so `cargo test clamp` runs
just the `clamp` fixture across both the raw and ts suites (both `space` and
`tab` variants).

## Architecture

The transform has two layers, and understanding the split matters when
changing behavior:

1. **`src/utils.rs`** -- pure string algorithm (`DeIndent` trait, `de_indent`
   method on `String`) that computes minimum indentation across lines and
   strips it. This has no knowledge of ASTs, comments, or SWC at all -- it's
   testable/reasoned about as plain string manipulation. `IndentStyle`
   (`Tab`/`Space`) picks which character counts as indentation; mixed
   indentation (e.g. a tab-indented line in space mode) is treated as _no_
   indentation for that line, per `get_line_indentation`.

2. **`src/visitor.rs`** -- the SWC `VisitMut` pass (`DeIndentVisitor`) that
   walks template literals (`Tpl` nodes), checks for a leading block comment
   matching the configured `tag`, and if found:
   - joins all the template's quasis (the literal text chunks between
     `${...}` interpolations) with a magic separator string
     (`$$--JOIN_QUASI--$$`),
   - runs the joined string through `de_indent` as a single unit (so
     indentation is computed across the _whole_ template, not per-quasi),
   - splits back on the separator and reassigns each quasi's `raw` value.

This join/split-around-interpolations dance is the key non-obvious trick in
this file -- it's necessary so indentation detection isn't fooled by quasi
boundaries falling mid-line.

`src/lib.rs` wires these together: `process_transform` (the `#[plugin_transform]`
entry point SWC's plugin runtime calls) parses the JSON plugin config into
`DeIndentVisitorConfig` and runs the visitor. `de_indent(...)` is also
exported as a plain `Pass` constructor for use in Rust-level tests
(`tests/ts_fixture.rs`) via `swc_ecma_transforms_testing::test_fixture`,
without going through the wasm plugin boundary.

## Testing conventions

There are two independent fixture suites under `tests/fixture/`, each with
`space/` and `tab/` variants, both driven by the same set of example
names (`clamp`, `slot`, `useControllableState`, etc. -- these are lifted from
a real downstream React component library, used as realistic inputs):

- **`tests/raw_fixture.rs`** + `tests/fixture/raw/**/{input,output}.txt` --
  exercises `DeIndent::de_indent` directly on plain strings. Add a fixture
  here to test the string algorithm in isolation.
- **`tests/ts_fixture.rs`** + `tests/fixture/ts/**/{input,output}.ts` --
  exercises the full pipeline (parse TS/TSX -> run the `VisitMut` pass via
  `de_indent()` -> codegen) via `swc_ecma_transforms_testing::test_fixture`.
  Add a fixture here to test comment detection + AST-level behavior
  end-to-end. Note the codegen output is intentionally compact/minified
  (SWC's default test codegen), not pretty-printed -- don't hand-format
  `output.ts` files, generate them by running the test and copying actual
  output once you've confirmed it's correct.

New fixtures are picked up automatically by the `#[testing::fixture(glob)]`
macro (no need to register new test fns) -- just add a new
`tests/fixture/{raw,ts}/{space,tab}/<name>/{input,output}.{txt,ts}` pair.

`.editorconfig` enforces tab indentation specifically for files under
`tests/fixture/**/tab/**/*`, and `.prettierignore` excludes `tests/fixture/**/*.ts`
from Prettier -- fixture files' exact whitespace is the point of the test and
must not be reformatted.

## Versioning & publishing

- `Cargo.toml`'s `version` is kept in sync with `package.json`'s `version` by
  convention (see comment in `Cargo.toml`), even though the crate itself is
  never published to crates.io (`publish = false`). `package.json`'s version
  is the one that matters -- it's what's published to npm.
- Releases are cut by pushing a tag matching `v<package.json version>` (e.g.
  `git tag v1.5.1 && git push origin v1.5.1`), which triggers
  `.github/workflows/publish.yml`. That workflow verifies the tag matches
  `package.json`'s version before publishing, builds the wasm artifact, and
  publishes via npm's **Trusted Publisher (OIDC)** flow -- no `NPM_TOKEN`
  secret is used or needed.
- `package.json`'s `repository.url` field must stay accurate and present:
  npm's provenance verification (used by trusted publishing) rejects
  publishes if it can't cross-check `repository.url` against the GitHub repo
  the OIDC token was minted from.
